name: Tech and Venture
summary: Covers venture and venture-style equity in technology companies from pre-seed to late stage: priced rounds and SAFE or convertible-note financings in SaaS, marketplaces, consumer apps, deep tech and hardware, AI, games and fintech. The base case for a venture-backed company is failure (about 75% never return cash), so the diligence spine is: rebuild every metric (ARR, NRR, GRR, CAC, gross margin, cohorts) from raw contracts, billings and bank deposits; reconcile every instrument on the cap table to signed documents; walk the IP assignment chain; test the core technical claim and a sample of live users yourself; map every investor veto and insider conflict; and price the specific security being bought, not the headline post-money or the last round.
one_check: If the company cannot produce customers acquired and total active customers (and, for non-subscription businesses, orders) by period, you cannot value it on fundamentals; rebuild cohort value (CBCV) from that file, reconciled to billings and bank deposits, before pricing.

subtypes.name: Pre-seed / seed
subtypes.description: SAFEs, convertible notes or a first priced round; little or no revenue. Diligence weight on founders (prior outcomes from cap tables), IP assignment, cap-table hygiene and runway to Series A at the 616-day seed-to-A cadence.

subtypes.name: Series A
subtypes.description: First institutional priced round on NVCA documents. Cap-table reconciliation of every pre-seed SAFE and grant before the term sheet; early cohort and retention data; runway of at least 24 months.

subtypes.name: Series B and later / late stage / secondaries
subtypes.description: Growth and late-stage rounds and secondaries. Adds QoE (AUP scope), Rule of 40 as a primary screen above about $25M ARR, finance-function and audit requirements (named CFO and controller, internal audit, audit committee), down-round and 2021-mark repricing, and the security-level valuation of a preference stack.

subtypes.name: SaaS / subscription software
subtypes.description: Recurring-revenue software. ARR rebuilt from contracts and billings; NRR and GRR from raw cohorts including churned logos; CAC payback, magic number, burn multiple and Rule of 40 benchmarks by ARR band.

subtypes.name: Marketplace
subtypes.description: Two-sided or transactional platforms. Cohort inputs include orders or transactions per period; CBCV applies; live-transaction sampling in production systems.

subtypes.name: Consumer app / consumer subscription
subtypes.description: Consumer software, games and subscription apps. Live-user sampling through production systems (Frank / JPMorgan), cohort repeat curves against the category leader, share of revenue from new customers (Blue Apron, Wayfair).

subtypes.name: Deep tech / hardware / life-science tools
subtypes.description: Companies whose value rests on a core scientific, hardware or device claim. Independent technical validation by an expert we hire, on our samples, in our presence; error rates, complaint logs, regulator correspondence; direct calls to every named validator, partner and government user (Theranos).

subtypes.name: AI / ML
subtypes.description: AI-first companies. Model and training-data provenance, NVCA 2025 national-security and OISP representations (foreign-person links, data categories, compute locations), independent validation of model performance claims, and theme-peak valuation discipline.

intake_questions.question: What is being sold: a priced preferred round, a SAFE, a convertible note, or a secondary sale of existing shares?
intake_questions.why: Sets the instrument to value and which NVCA documents and conversion mechanics apply.

intake_questions.question: What stage is the round: pre-seed/seed, Series A, or Series B and later?
intake_questions.why: Drives stage subtype (seed, series-a, series-b-plus) and stage-specific checks (finance function, QoE, Rule of 40).

intake_questions.question: What is the business model: SaaS/subscription, marketplace, consumer app, deep tech/hardware, or AI?
intake_questions.why: Drives business-model subtypes and which metrics (ARR/NRR, orders per period, technical validation, model provenance) apply.

intake_questions.question: What is current ARR (or annualized revenue)? Is it above about $25M?
intake_questions.why: Below about $25M ARR underwrite growth plus NRR/GRR and burn; above it the Rule of 40 becomes a primary screen (ICONIQ 2025).

intake_questions.question: Does the company's value depend on a core scientific, hardware, medical or model-performance claim that has not been independently validated?
intake_questions.why: Triggers independent technical validation on our samples in our presence (Theranos).

intake_questions.question: Who leads the round, which existing investors are participating, and are insiders on both sides of the price?
intake_questions.why: Triggers the insider-round checklist (Footprint) and lead-investor diligence-effort benchmark.

intake_questions.question: Is any strategic or corporate VC investor on the cap table, and does any investor hold a veto over financing, debt or M&A?
intake_questions.why: Triggers the investor-rights map and catch-and-kill review (Zync v. Porsche).

intake_questions.question: Was any prior round priced in 2021 or earlier, and is the proposed price justified by the last round?
intake_questions.why: Triggers repricing against current comparables and a down-round model.

intake_questions.question: Is the company in a theme that has recently peaked in media attention or fund launches (AI, crypto, space, climate)?
intake_questions.why: Triggers theme-timing comparison of entry valuation (Ben-David et al.).

intake_questions.question: Does the company process personal data, operate in a regulated domain, or have foreign-person investors or offshore compute?
intake_questions.why: Triggers privacy, regulator correspondence and NVCA national-security/OISP representations.

intake_questions.question: Where is the company's cash held, and is there any loan covenant requiring exclusive banking?

requests.request: Provide the pitch deck and all written investor materials as sent to other investors.
requests.format: Final PDF versions with send dates; any versions shown to other investors.
requests.why: Charisma bias: pitch delivery predicts funding but not outcomes.
requests.pass: Materials scored by at least two raters against a fixed rubric before any live pitch; every quantitative claim tagged to a data-room source.
requests.fail: Claims with no data-room source; materials that differ from versions sent to others.
requests.verify: We score independently before meeting; cross-check claims against data room.

requests.request: Provide the 3 to 5 year financial model with all assumptions and the scenario tab.
requests.format: Native spreadsheet with live formulas; monthly for 24 months, then annual.
requests.why: Padded projections: 90% to 95% of VC-backed companies miss a declared projection.
requests.pass: Model runs; every driver sourced; management's ranges are shown so we can widen them about 2x; margins flat unless a named cost line falls.
requests.fail: Hard-coded outputs, margin expansion with no named cost line, hockey-stick revenue with no acquisition and retention drivers.
requests.verify: We rebuild the base case from cohorts and widen ranges about 2x (Ben-David, Graham and Harvey).

requests.request: Provide the fully diluted cap table listing every share, option, RSU, SAFE, warrant, convertible note, side letter and any benefit-fund issuance, with holder and terms.
requests.format: Native spreadsheet or cap-table platform export (e.g. Carta) with instrument-level detail and a conversion model for every SAFE and note at this round's price.
requests.why: Cap-table disasters from unpapered SAFEs and grants surfacing at Series A.
requests.pass: Every instrument listed with holder, date, amount, price or cap, discount, and conversion result; totals tie to the charter's authorized shares.
requests.fail: Instruments missing, conversion not modeled, or totals that do not tie.
requests.verify: Reconcile line by line to signed instruments (see confirmatory reconciliation item).

requests.request: Grant read-only access to the raw data room: contracts, billing-system exports, general ledger and bank portals.
requests.format: Virtual data room plus read-only credentials to billing system and bank portals.
requests.why: 'Trust the deck' metrics.
requests.pass: Access granted before the term sheet; raw data, not summaries.
requests.fail: Founder refuses raw access or offers only summaries.
requests.verify: We log in ourselves and pull exports directly.

requests.request: Provide the customer-cohort input file: customers acquired per period and total active customers per period, by month or quarter since inception; for non-subscription businesses also orders or transactions per period.
requests.format: CSV export from the production database or billing system, with query text; monthly preferred.
requests.why: No cohort file, no valuation on fundamentals (THE ONE CHECK).
requests.pass: File delivered within days, covering every period since launch, and reconciling to reported revenue within 2%.
requests.fail: Company cannot or will not produce acquired and active counts by period.
requests.verify: Our engineer reruns the query against production; reconcile totals to billings.

requests.request: Provide current cash position and default-alive runway: monthly burn for the trailing 12 months and forecast to the next round.
requests.format: Bank-confirmed balances at a stated date plus monthly cash-flow statement.
requests.why: Running out of cash before the next round at today's slower cadence.
requests.pass: Runway of at least 24 months to the next round (616-day seed-to-A median, 696 days between rounds, plus six months buffer), or a default-alive path.
requests.fail: Runway under 24 months with no default-alive path; burn that does not tie to bank outflows.
requests.verify: Tie burn to bank statements; recompute runway ourselves.

requests.request: Provide a treasury map: every bank and investment account with balance by institution, insured share, and any loan covenant requiring exclusive banking.
requests.format: Schedule plus month-end statements for each account.
requests.why: Uninsured cash stranded at a failed bank (SVB).
requests.pass: No more than one quarter of payroll uninsured at any single bank; balances above $250,000 spread across banks, insured sweeps or Treasury MMFs; no exclusive-banking covenant, or one waived.
requests.fail: More than one quarter of payroll uninsured at one bank; single-bank covenant.
requests.verify: Bank confirmations; read covenant text in loan agreements.

requests.request: Provide a round-process statement: who sourced the deal, who else was offered the round, whether a banker ran it, and any competing term sheets.
requests.format: Written statement signed by the CEO, with names of investors approached.
requests.why: 'Proprietary deal' assertions hide adverse selection.
requests.pass: Names of other investors approached and outcome; consistent with what co-investors tell us.
requests.fail: Refusal to say who else saw it.
requests.verify: Call one or two named investors who passed.

requests.request: Provide the lead investor's diligence record for this round: days from first contact, hours of diligence, management in-person hours, sites visited and reference calls made.
requests.format: Written summary from the lead investor; reference-call list.
requests.why: A thin lead is not a diligence anchor; diligence falls in hot markets.
requests.pass: At or near benchmark: about 83 days, about 118 hours, about 10 reference calls (13 late-stage, 8 early-stage).
requests.fail: A fraction of benchmark effort; diligence shortened because the round is competitive.
requests.verify: Ask the lead directly; we hold our own diligence floor regardless.

requests.request: Provide the lead investor's and named co-investors' deal-level track record, attributed to the leading partner, with and without the top one or two outcomes, stated as PME.
requests.format: Deal-level table with entry and exit dates, cash flows and leading partner.
requests.why: Persistence comes from access, not picking; a 'consistent singles' thesis contradicts the base rate.
requests.pass: Track record attributed to partners still at the firm; record reported without compounding IRR or comparing IRR with time-weighted indices.
requests.fail: Record attributable to departed partners; only compounded IRRs shown.
requests.verify: Cross-check against fund reports and Chapter 10 manager diligence.

requests.request: Provide the lead investor's monitoring capacity: board seats held by the deal partner, travel distance to the company, and partner bandwidth.
requests.format: List of the partner's current board seats and location.
requests.why: Monitoring matters: proximity raised odds of successful exit by 1.0 to 1.4 points.
requests.pass: Deal partner has capacity to attend board meetings in person.
requests.fail: Partner over-boarded or remote with no plan for monitoring.
requests.verify: Check partner's board list against public sources.

requests.request: Provide each founder's prior companies with role and actual investor outcome, backed by cap tables, exit documents or filings.
requests.format: Cap tables or filings for each prior company.
requests.why: 'Prior exit' is often inflated; prior success changes base rates (30% vs 18%).
requests.pass: Outcomes per filings and cap tables match the bio.
requests.fail: Bio outcome not supported by documents.
requests.verify: Search filings and call prior investors.

requests.request: Provide the valuation rationale: comparables used, their dates, and how the price relates to the last round and to the sector's history.
requests.format: Memo with comparable set and sources.
requests.why: Marking off the last round or buying a theme at its peak.
requests.pass: Price supported by current comparables, not the last round; entry valuation compared with sector history and the theme's media and fund-launch peak.
requests.fail: Price justified only by the last round or theme momentum.
requests.verify: We pull our own comparables and theme timing data.

requests.request: Provide the investment thesis stating what makes this company different from the base rate (about 75% never return cash).
requests.format: Written thesis by the sponsor bringing the deal.
requests.why: IC memo must state the prior before the argument.
requests.pass: Thesis names evidenced differences (retention, unit economics, validated technology).
requests.fail: Thesis rests on team charisma or market size alone.
requests.verify: Test each claimed difference against data-room evidence.

requests.request: Provide the draft term sheet, identifying the NVCA model version it is based on.
requests.format: Draft in Word with redline against the NVCA model term sheet in force at signing.
requests.why: Off-market terms hidden in non-standard drafting.
requests.pass: Based on the current nvca.org model set; deviations listed.
requests.fail: Non-NVCA drafting with unexplained deviations.
requests.verify: Compare against nvca.org model documents directly.

requests.request: Provide the SAFE or convertible-note form for this financing with valuation cap, discount, MFN and conversion terms.
requests.format: Executable form plus a conversion model at plausible next-round prices.
requests.why: Unmodeled SAFE dilution surfacing at the next priced round.
requests.pass: Conversion modeled at three next-round prices; dilution to our position stated.
requests.fail: Uncapped or stacked instruments with unmodeled conversion.

requests.request: Provide the full preference stack: liquidation preference, participation, seniority and dividends for every series.
requests.format: Charter excerpt and a waterfall model at several exit values.
requests.why: Headline post-money overstates value when preferences, ratchets or participation exist.
requests.pass: Our security's value computed from the waterfall; 1x non-participating preferred; no senior 2x participating series.
requests.fail: 2x participating preference or senior stacking that impairs our security.
requests.verify: Rebuild the waterfall from the charter text.

requests.request: Provide anti-dilution terms for every series.
requests.format: Charter excerpt.
requests.why: Full ratchets punish later investors and founders.
requests.pass: Broad-based weighted average.
requests.fail: Full ratchet in any series.

requests.request: Provide the proposed board composition, protective provisions and drag-along terms.
requests.format: Term sheet sections and voting agreement draft.
requests.why: Control terms that block financing or exit.
requests.pass: Board not wholly founder-controlled at late stage; protective provisions standard per NVCA; drag-along with customary protections.
requests.fail: Board fully founder-controlled; protective provisions giving a single holder a financing or M&A veto.
requests.verify: Compare to NVCA voting agreement and charter models.

requests.request: Provide pro rata, redemption, dividend, option-pool and vesting terms with a note on which points the lead negotiated hardest.
requests.format: Term sheet and negotiation summary from the lead.
requests.why: Atypical negotiation patterns signal hidden issues.
requests.pass: Negotiation pattern consistent with the VC map (least flexible on pro rata, preference, anti-dilution, valuation, board, vesting).
requests.fail: Lead concedes preference or board control but fights on dividends, without explanation.

requests.request: Provide a fully diluted share count including options, RSUs, warrants, SAFEs and benefit-fund issuance, and the implied price per fully diluted share.
requests.format: Schedule tying to the cap table.
requests.why: Implied valuation understated by ignoring dilution (one case moved from $1.25T to about $1.7T).
requests.pass: Fully diluted count ties to cap table; reverse valuation states the steady-state margin, growth and pricing power required, and they are achievable against comparables.
requests.fail: Basic share count used; required steady-state economics implausible.
requests.verify: Recompute from cap table and option ledger.

requests.request: Provide an investor-rights map: every investor veto or consent right over financing, debt and M&A, who holds it, every board designee, and every time such a right has been exercised.
requests.format: Table citing the charter, voting agreement, IRA, notes and side letters by section.
requests.why: Vetoes used to block financings and catch-and-kill (Zync v. Porsche).
requests.pass: Complete map; no strategic investor holds a financing or M&A veto, or it is waived before closing.
requests.fail: Strategic holds a veto over financing or M&A; history of a right being used against the company.
requests.verify: Rebuild the map ourselves from the signed documents.

requests.request: Provide every strategic and corporate VC investor's information, observer, ROFR and ROFN rights and any commercial agreements with the company.
requests.format: Signed agreements and side letters.
requests.why: Technology leakage and exit blocking; CVCs leave after a median four years.
requests.pass: No ROFR/ROFN on a sale of the company; information rights ring-fenced for competitively sensitive data; no reliance on CVC follow-on.
requests.fail: ROFR on company sale; unrestricted information rights to a competitor.

requests.request: Provide the voting-control structure: every share class's votes per share, any super-voting class and its sunset.
requests.format: Charter excerpts and voting agreements.
requests.why: Founder super-voting control without a sunset (Theranos: 100 votes per share).
requests.pass: Super-voting class, if any, has a time or event sunset, and is priced.
requests.fail: Super-voting control with no sunset.

requests.request: If insiders are on both sides of the round: provide the list of conflicted directors and the composition and mandate of any independent committee.
requests.format: Board resolution forming the committee; conflicts schedule.
requests.why: Entire-fairness exposure and dilution of non-insiders (Footprint).
requests.pass: Independent committee with its own advisors approved the terms.
requests.fail: No independent committee; conflicted designees voted.

requests.request: If insiders are on both sides of the round: provide evidence of third-party price discovery (outside lead, competing term sheets) and the reasons any alternative was rejected.
requests.format: Term sheets received and board materials.
requests.why: Insider round priced below market.
requests.pass: At least one outside price signal or a documented market check.
requests.fail: Higher-valuation alternatives set aside without reasons.

requests.request: If insiders are on both sides of the round: provide each insider fund's latest mark of the company and the conversion terms of any insider bridge.
requests.format: Fund-report excerpts and bridge notes.
requests.why: Round priced at about half the funds' own implied value (Footprint).
requests.pass: Round price not below insiders' latest marks or bridge-implied values, or the gap is explained.
requests.fail: Price materially below insiders' own marks.
requests.verify: Request marks from the funds' LP reports.

requests.request: If insiders are on both sides of the round: provide the timeline and information package given to non-participating holders, and what happens to non-participants (pay-to-play, conversion to common, preference stacking).
requests.format: Notice to holders and data-room access logs.
requests.why: Three-week windows and missing disclosures support fiduciary claims.
requests.pass: Non-participants get weeks, the same information as insiders, and disclosure of valuation, insider benefits and rejected offers.
requests.fail: Short window, information asymmetry, punitive pay-to-play.

requests.request: Provide the board minutes recording alternatives considered for this round and every prior bridge or down round.
requests.format: Signed minutes.
requests.why: No record of alternatives undermines the fairness record.
requests.pass: Minutes list each alternative and why it was rejected.
requests.fail: Minutes silent on alternatives.
requests.verify: Read minutes; compare with term sheets received.

requests.request: Provide the history of every prior round, bridge and down round with price, lead and terms; for any 2021-vintage round provide current comparables.
requests.format: Financing history table with signed documents.
requests.why: Last-round marks are not marks (FTX $32B; Stripe about half its 2021 value).
requests.pass: Prior marks repriced to current comparables; a down-round case modeled.
requests.fail: Price justified by a 2021 mark.

requests.request: Provide use of proceeds and the milestones the round must reach before the next financing.
requests.format: Budget by function and milestone plan.
requests.why: Capital spent on irreversible commitments before demand is validated (Webvan).
requests.pass: Milestones evidence-based and reachable within runway; no large irreversible commitments before demand is validated.
requests.fail: Proceeds funding irreversible build-out ahead of demand evidence.
requests.verify: Compare budget to cohort and pipeline data.

requests.request: Provide a downside case built from base rates, with management's ranges widened about 2x and, if the round is priced in a hot market, a wider downside still.
requests.format: Model tab with explicit assumptions.
requests.why: Hot-market startups are both likelier to fail and to be extreme successes; the round price is not validation.
requests.pass: Downside case exists, uses base-rate revenue and retention, and the round still survives (no wipe-out of our security at the downside exit value).
requests.fail: Only a sponsor case; downside narrower than management's own range.
requests.verify: We build our own downside from cohorts and base rates.

requests.request: Provide the long-run market model: expected steady-state market size, the company's share of it, and the path back to today, benchmarked against historical high-growth companies.
requests.format: Model tab and sources.
requests.why: DCFs that extrapolate history.
requests.pass: Path from steady state back to today is consistent with historical high-growth trajectories.
requests.fail: Valuation built by extrapolating recent growth.
requests.verify: Benchmark path against public high-growth histories.

requests.request: Provide the exit analysis: named likely acquirers or IPO path, any acquirer with an overlapping product, and HSR and antitrust considerations.
requests.format: Memo.
requests.why: Exit to a strategic with an overlapping product faces sub-HSR scrutiny and shelving risk (killer acquisitions).
requests.pass: Exit thesis does not rely on a single overlapping strategic; antitrust risk stated.
requests.fail: Exit depends on an overlapping strategic with no antitrust analysis.

requests.request: Provide the full set of contracts that shape the deal beyond the term sheet: investor, channel and employee agreements with change-of-control, exclusivity or economic terms.
requests.format: Executed contracts list with key terms.
requests.why: Sahlman: the deal is the full set of contracts, not just the term sheet.
requests.pass: No contract transfers material economics or control away from the company or new investors.
requests.fail: Undisclosed channel exclusivity or employee change-of-control payouts.

requests.request: Provide the charter (certificate of incorporation) and bylaws with every amendment.
requests.format: Certified copies from the state of incorporation plus company copies.
requests.why: Unauthorized issuances; terms that differ from the summary.
requests.pass: Certified charter matches the cap table's classes and authorized shares.
requests.fail: Mismatch between charter and cap table.
requests.verify: Order certified copies from the Secretary of State.

requests.request: Provide every board and stockholder consent and minutes since formation.
requests.format: Signed consents and minutes.
requests.why: Unapproved grants or financings.
requests.pass: Every issuance on the cap table has an approving consent.
requests.fail: Issuances without approval.
requests.verify: Match each consent to cap-table entries.

requests.request: Provide every prior financing document: each SAFE, convertible note, warrant, stock purchase agreement and side letter, fully executed.
requests.format: Executed PDFs.
requests.why: Unpapered or late-surfacing instruments.
requests.pass: Every instrument on the cap table has an executed document and vice versa.
requests.fail: Any instrument without a document, or a document not on the cap table.

requests.request: Provide a line-by-line reconciliation of the cap table to signed documents, with an officer's certificate that the side-letter list is complete.
requests.format: Reconciliation workbook referencing each document; signed officer certificate.
requests.why: The single biggest preventable mess in venture.
requests.pass: Zero unreconciled items before the term sheet is signed.
requests.fail: Unreconciled items or side letters surfacing late.
requests.verify: Company counsel confirms; we re-perform a sample.

requests.request: Provide each founder's and early employee's 83(b) election with proof of timely IRS filing.
requests.format: Copies with certified-mail receipt or IRS acknowledgement.
requests.why: Tax exposure on unvested founder stock.
requests.pass: Filed within 30 days of grant for every restricted-stock holder.
requests.fail: Missing or late 83(b) elections.

requests.request: Provide the equity incentive plan, every grant agreement, board approvals and 409A valuations.
requests.format: Executed plan and grants; 409A reports.
requests.why: Unapproved or mispriced grants.
requests.pass: Every grant approved and priced at or above the 409A in effect.
requests.fail: Grants below 409A or unapproved.
requests.verify: Tie grants to option ledger and consents.

requests.request: Provide all voting agreements, stockholder agreements and ROFR and co-sale agreements in force.
requests.format: Executed copies.
requests.why: Hidden control arrangements.
requests.pass: Agreements consistent with the investor-rights map.
requests.fail: Undisclosed voting arrangements.

requests.request: Provide executed IP assignment (CIIAA or equivalent) agreements from every founder.
requests.format: Executed agreements including pre-incorporation assignments.
requests.why: A founder who never assigned IP is a deal-killer.
requests.pass: Every founder has assigned all company-related IP, including pre-formation work.
requests.fail: Any founder without an assignment.
requests.verify: IP counsel review; compare to founders and early repository contributors.

requests.request: Provide executed IP assignment agreements from every employee and contractor who contributed code, designs, data or inventions, with a list of all contributors.
requests.format: Executed agreements plus repository contributor list.
requests.why: Contractor-owned IP.
requests.pass: Every contributor on the repository and payroll/AP lists has a present-tense assignment.
requests.fail: Contributors without assignments.
requests.verify: Our tech reviewer extracts the contributor list from the repository; match to agreements.

requests.request: Provide a schedule of patents, patent applications, trademarks and domain names with ownership and status.
requests.format: Schedule plus USPTO and registry records.
requests.why: IP held by founders or third parties.
requests.pass: Registered owner is the company for every item.
requests.fail: IP registered to a founder or affiliate.

requests.request: Provide an open-source component inventory with licenses, generated by a scanning tool.
requests.format: SBOM or scan output (e.g. software composition analysis) for every shipped product.
requests.why: Copyleft license exposure in proprietary code.
requests.pass: No copyleft components in distributed proprietary code without compliance.
requests.fail: Undisclosed copyleft in distributed code.
requests.verify: Third-party tech diligence rescans the repository.

requests.request: Provide material contracts: top customer contracts, partner, channel, supplier and licensing agreements.
requests.format: Executed copies with amendments.
requests.why: Contracts that differ from presented terms; termination rights.
requests.pass: Terms match ARR schedule; no undisclosed termination for convenience or change of control.
requests.fail: Material contract terms differ from the ARR schedule.
requests.verify: Read contracts against the ARR schedule.

requests.request: Provide a schedule of litigation, threatened claims and demand letters.
requests.format: Schedule plus pleadings; counsel letter.
requests.why: Undisclosed claims.
requests.pass: All matters disclosed and reserved.
requests.fail: Undisclosed matters found in docket searches.

requests.request: Provide all regulator correspondence, inspection reports and filings for regulated products or activities.
requests.format: Complete correspondence file.
requests.why: Regulatory problems hidden behind claims of approval (Theranos).
requests.pass: No unresolved adverse findings; claimed approvals confirmed with the regulator.
requests.fail: Undisclosed adverse correspondence.
requests.verify: Search regulator databases and ask the regulator where possible.

requests.request: Provide responses to NVCA 2025 national-security and OISP representations: foreign-person investors and links, sensitive data categories held, and compute and data-hosting locations.
requests.format: Completed questionnaire signed by an officer, with cloud contracts showing regions.
requests.why: CFIUS and outbound-investment exposure.
requests.pass: Reps can be given without exception, or exceptions are cleared by counsel.
requests.fail: Undisclosed foreign-person control links or sensitive data hosted offshore.
requests.verify: Counsel review; check cloud-provider region settings.

requests.request: Provide a contract-level ARR and MRR schedule: every customer, contract start and end, ACV, billing frequency, discounts and renewal status.
requests.format: Native spreadsheet tied to contract IDs.
requests.why: Revenue-quality fiction: ARR that is non-recurring or uncollected.
requests.pass: ARR rebuilt from contracts equals reported ARR within 2%; non-recurring items excluded.
requests.fail: Rebuilt ARR materially below reported; one-off revenue counted as ARR.

requests.request: Provide billing-system exports of every invoice and credit note for the trailing 24 months.
requests.format: Direct export from the billing system (Stripe, NetSuite, Chargebee or similar) with read-only access.
requests.why: Revenue that exists only in the deck.
requests.pass: Invoices tie to the ARR schedule and to cash collections.
requests.fail: Invoices missing for reported ARR.
requests.verify: Pull exports ourselves via read-only access.

requests.request: Provide a monthly reconciliation of billings and collections to bank deposits for the trailing 24 months.
requests.format: Reconciliation workbook with bank statements.
requests.why: Revenue not collected in cash.
requests.pass: Deposits reconcile to billings within 2% each month; no unexplained related-party receipts.
requests.fail: Unreconciled gaps; collections well below billings.

requests.request: Provide historical financial statements (audited if available) and monthly management accounts for the trailing 36 months or since inception.
requests.format: Audited statements with auditor's report; monthly P&L, balance sheet and cash flow.
requests.why: Unreliable books.
requests.pass: Statements tie to GL and bank; late stage audited by a firm sized for the company.
requests.fail: No financial statements, or numbers that change between versions.
requests.verify: Tie to GL and bank statements.

requests.request: Provide the revenue recognition policy and any changes over time.
requests.format: Written policy approved by the CFO or auditor.
requests.why: Aggressive recognition inflating ARR.
requests.pass: Policy consistent with ASC 606 and consistently applied.
requests.fail: Policy changes that flatter recent periods.

requests.request: Provide a monthly customer-level revenue file since inception, including every churned customer, for NRR, GRR and churn rebuild.
requests.format: CSV from billing system.
requests.why: NRR that excludes churned logos.
requests.pass: Our rebuilt NRR and GRR match reported within one point; benchmark NRR against private median just above 100% (top quartile 117%) and GRR near 85% to 90%.
requests.fail: Reported NRR exceeds rebuilt NRR by more than one point; churned logos excluded.
requests.verify: Rebuild ourselves; reconcile cohort revenue to billings and deposits.

requests.request: Provide cumulative revenue and gross profit per acquisition cohort by period since acquisition.
requests.format: Cohort matrix from production data.
requests.why: Collapsing cohorts hidden by growth (Blue Apron).
requests.pass: Each new cohort at least as valuable as the last; curves flatten (Harry's, Dollar Shave Club pattern).
requests.fail: Each recent cohort worth less than the last.

requests.request: Provide the share of each period's revenue that came from customers acquired in that period.
requests.format: Schedule by month or quarter.
requests.why: A hockey stick made entirely of acquisition (Wayfair).
requests.pass: Share of revenue from new customers stable or falling while repeat holds.
requests.fail: Rising share of revenue from new customers with flat repeat.

requests.request: Provide spend per order and gross margin by cohort, and repeat-purchase rates by cohort age.
requests.format: Cohort-level schedule.
requests.why: Repeat rates below the category leader.
requests.pass: Repeat at each cohort age at or near the category leader at the same age.
requests.fail: Repeat materially below the category leader.

requests.request: Provide sales and marketing spend by channel by month, with new customers by channel, to compute paid CAC unblended and CAC payback by segment.
requests.format: Ad-platform exports, payroll for sales staff, GL detail.
requests.why: Blended CAC hiding paid CAC.
requests.pass: Paid CAC payback within SMB under 12, mid-market under 18, enterprise under 24 months (median 16, IQR 10 to 24); LTV:CAC above 3:1 recomputed from cohorts (WEAK).
requests.fail: Payback outside targets or only blended CAC available.
requests.verify: Recompute from ad-platform and GL data.

requests.request: Provide quarterly net new ARR, net burn and S&M spend to compute burn multiple and magic number.
requests.format: Quarterly schedule tied to GL and ARR schedule.
requests.why: Inefficient growth.
requests.pass: Burn multiple under 1.5x (above 3x is trouble) and magic number above 0.75 (both WEAK practitioner benchmarks).
requests.fail: Burn multiple above 3x.
requests.verify: Recompute from GL and ARR rebuild.

requests.request: Provide gross margin build: COGS detail (hosting, third-party fees, support, implementation) by month.
requests.format: GL detail and vendor invoices.
requests.why: Gross margin flattered by misclassifying COGS.
requests.pass: Gross margin toward 65% to 70% long-run, top performers 80%+ (v1 practitioner 70% to 75%).
requests.fail: Hosting or support costs below the line.

requests.request: Provide, for companies above about $25M ARR, the Rule of 40 calculation (YoY ARR growth plus FCF margin) for the last eight quarters.
requests.format: Quarterly schedule tied to ARR rebuild and cash flow statement.
requests.why: Inefficient growth at scale.
requests.pass: 40% or more (median 38% Q1 2026, WEAK); growth weighted about 2x margin.
requests.fail: Below 40% with no path.
requests.verify: Recompute from rebuilt ARR and bank-tied FCF.

requests.request: Provide a line-by-line cost bridge for any margin expansion in the plan, naming each cost line that falls as a share of revenue and the evidence (contracts, supplier quotes).
requests.format: Schedule with supporting contracts or quotes.
requests.why: Projected margin expansion with no named driver.
requests.pass: Each efficiency named and supported; otherwise base case holds margins flat.
requests.fail: Margin expansion with no named line.

requests.request: Provide management's forecast ranges (base, upside, downside) with the confidence they attach.
requests.format: Scenario tab and narrative.
requests.why: Overconfident ranges (36% hit rate on 80% intervals).
requests.pass: Ranges provided so we can widen them about 2x.
requests.fail: Single-point forecast only.

requests.request: Provide customer concentration: revenue by customer for the top 20 and share of total.
requests.format: Schedule tied to billing data.
requests.why: Concentrated revenue presented as ARR.
requests.pass: No single customer above 25% of revenue presented as ARR.
requests.fail: One customer above 25%.

requests.request: Provide the sales pipeline with stage, value, expected close and historical conversion rates.
requests.format: CRM export.
requests.why: Pipeline padding.
requests.pass: Historical conversion supports forecast.
requests.fail: Forecast conversion above history.

requests.request: Provide all debt, venture-debt and loan agreements with covenants.
requests.format: Executed agreements.
requests.why: Exclusive-banking covenants and hidden leverage.
requests.pass: No exclusive-banking covenant without insured sweep; covenants in compliance.
requests.fail: Covenant breach or exclusive-banking requirement.

requests.request: Provide the finance-function roster: named CFO and controller with their prior public- or audited-company experience, internal audit or equivalent, and audit-committee composition.
requests.format: CVs, org chart, audit committee charter.
requests.why: Late-stage companies lacking a controller (FTX: no internal audit, no accounting department).
requests.pass: Named CFO and controller with audited-company experience; internal audit or equivalent; audit committee; board not wholly founder-controlled.
requests.fail: No controller; no internal audit; no audit committee at late stage.
requests.verify: Interview CFO and controller; call the auditor.

requests.request: Provide a complete employee census reconciled to payroll.
requests.format: HRIS export and payroll register for the same date.
requests.why: No complete employee list (FTX).
requests.pass: Census ties to payroll one for one.
requests.fail: Employees on payroll not on census or vice versa.

requests.request: Provide the schedule of any customer assets, deposits or funds held for customers and show where they sit on the balance sheet.
requests.format: Balance-sheet detail and custodial agreements.
requests.why: Customer deposits held off the main balance sheet (FTX).
requests.pass: Customer assets and liabilities recorded on the balance sheet and segregated.
requests.fail: Customer funds off balance sheet or commingled.

requests.request: Provide a list of every named marquee customer, partner, validator and government user cited in investor materials, with permission to contact each directly.
requests.format: List with counterparty names; we source contacts independently.
requests.why: Fabricated endorsements (Theranos pharma logos; DoD medevac claim).
requests.pass: Every named counterparty confirms the relationship as described.
requests.fail: Company refuses contact or a counterparty denies the claim.
requests.verify: We call using contacts sourced independently, not via the company.

requests.request: Provide customer references sufficient for about 10 reference calls (13 late stage, 8 early stage), including churned customers.
requests.format: Names and contacts; we add customers chosen from the billing file.
requests.why: Reference lists curated by the company.
requests.pass: Calls completed at benchmark count, including customers we picked and at least one churned customer.
requests.fail: Company-picked references only.
requests.verify: Pick references ourselves from the customer file.

requests.request: Grant our engineer supervised read access to production systems to test a random sample of claimed users or customers for live activity (logins, transactions, deliverable email).
requests.format: Live session with our engineer present; query logs retained.
requests.why: Fabricated users (Frank: 4M synthetic customers; about 70% of emails bounced).
requests.pass: Random sample shows live activity at rates consistent with reported active users.
requests.fail: Refusal, or sampled users inactive or non-existent.
requests.verify: Our engineer draws the sample and runs queries.

requests.request: Provide the test protocol for the core technical claim and agree to independent validation on our samples, in our presence, by an expert we hire.
requests.format: Written protocol, equipment list and acceptance criteria.
requests.why: Technology that does not do what is claimed (Theranos ran about a dozen of about 200 promised tests).
requests.pass: Validation meets the stated protocol on our samples.
requests.fail: Refusal, or results below claimed performance.

requests.request: Provide error rates, test results and performance data for the product or model from production use.
requests.format: Raw logs or datasets, not summaries.
requests.why: Performance claims that differ from field reality.
requests.pass: Field error rates match claims.
requests.fail: Error rates withheld or worse than claimed.

requests.request: Provide customer complaint logs and the internal whistleblower or employee-concern log.
requests.format: Complete logs with resolution.
requests.why: Employees raised internal warnings at Theranos.
requests.pass: Complaints resolved; no pattern of unaddressed product or data-integrity concerns.
requests.fail: Recurring unresolved complaints or warnings.

requests.request: Grant code-repository and architecture-documentation access for code and architecture review.
requests.format: Read-only repository access and architecture diagrams.
requests.why: Unscalable or fragile technology.
requests.pass: No critical defects unaddressed in the reviewer's report.
requests.fail: Critical architecture or code-quality issues.

requests.request: Provide the security posture: latest penetration test, vulnerability scans, security policies and certifications (SOC 2 or ISO 27001 if held).
requests.format: Third-party reports and policies.
requests.why: Security weaknesses that become breaches.
requests.pass: No open critical or high findings.
requests.fail: Open critical findings.

requests.request: Provide the data map (personal and sensitive data held, where, and under which basis) and the security incident history.
requests.format: Data inventory and incident register.
requests.why: Privacy and breach exposure.
requests.pass: Data map complete; incidents disclosed and remediated.
requests.fail: Undisclosed incidents.
requests.verify: Search breach notifications; security reviewer validates.

requests.request: Provide AI model and data provenance: training data sources and licenses, model lineage, third-party models used, and evaluation results.
requests.format: Data-source register with licenses; model cards.
requests.why: Unlicensed training data and overstated model claims.
requests.pass: All training data licensed or owned; model claims reproducible.
requests.fail: Unlicensed or scraped data without rights.
requests.verify: IP counsel and tech reviewer verify.

requests.request: Provide the org chart and key employee agreements, including offer letters, non-competes and retention arrangements.
requests.format: Executed agreements.
requests.why: Key-person and retention risk.
requests.pass: Key employees signed; retention aligned with plan.
requests.fail: Key person without agreement.

requests.request: Provide each founder's vesting schedule, acceleration terms and current vested status.
requests.format: Restricted-stock agreements.
requests.why: Fully vested founders with no retention.
requests.pass: Meaningful unvested equity remains for each founder.
requests.fail: Fully vested founders with single-trigger acceleration.

requests.request: Provide the board roster with each director's domain expertise and committee roles.
requests.format: Board list with bios.
requests.why: Celebrity boards without domain or audit expertise (Theranos).
requests.pass: At least one director with domain expertise and one able to chair audit at late stage.
requests.fail: No domain experts; no audit-capable director.

requests.request: Provide a key-person risk assessment and succession plan for the founders and CTO.
requests.format: Written plan; key-person insurance if held.
requests.why: Key-person dependency.
requests.pass: Named successors or mitigation.
requests.fail: No plan.

requests.request: Sign the access letter for our tech and security diligence firm and provide the engineering leads for interviews.
requests.format: Executed access letter; interview schedule.
requests.why: Unverified technology claims.
requests.pass: Report delivered with no unresolved critical findings.
requests.fail: Access refused or critical findings.

requests.request: Provide our QoE provider access to GL, billing and bank data for an agreed-upon-procedures scope covering ARR, revenue cut-off and proof of cash.
requests.format: Engagement access; scope letter shared with us.
requests.why: Unverified growth-stage financials.
requests.pass: QoE completed with no material unreconciled items; scope states what was not tested.
requests.fail: Material unreconciled items or restricted scope.

requests.request: Provide IP counsel with the assignment chain, registrations and open-source scan for a chain-of-title review.
requests.format: Complete IP file.
requests.why: Missing assignments.
requests.pass: Counsel confirms unbroken chain of title.
requests.fail: Counsel identifies gaps.

requests.request: Provide signed consents for background checks on each founder and C-level executive.
requests.format: Signed FCRA-compliant consents.
requests.why: Undisclosed history.
requests.pass: No undisclosed adverse findings.
requests.fail: Undisclosed adverse findings.

requests.request: Provide samples, equipment access and a lab or test slot for our independent technical validator.
requests.format: Access confirmation and schedule.
requests.why: Fraudulent demos on third-party equipment.
requests.pass: Validation completed on the company's own device or model in our presence.
requests.fail: Demonstration on third-party equipment or refusal.
requests.verify: Validator hired and paid by us.

requests.request: Provide the pro forma closing cap table reflecting conversion of every SAFE and note, signed off by company counsel.
requests.format: Counsel-certified cap table.
requests.why: Closing on an unreconciled cap table.
requests.pass: Ties to reconciliation and conversion model with zero exceptions.
requests.fail: Any unreconciled item at closing.

requests.request: Deliver confirmatory IP assignments for every gap identified in diligence.
requests.format: Executed confirmatory assignments.
requests.why: Missing IP assignment.
requests.pass: Every gap closed before funding.
requests.fail: Any gap open at closing.

requests.request: Deliver the executed NVCA definitive documents: Stock Purchase Agreement, Amended Charter, Investors' Rights Agreement, Voting Agreement, ROFR and Co-Sale Agreement, Management Rights Letter and Indemnification Agreement.
requests.format: Executed documents; filed charter with state stamp.
requests.why: Terms drifting from the term sheet.
requests.pass: Documents match the agreed term sheet and the NVCA version in force at signing.
requests.fail: Deviations from term sheet.
requests.verify: Our counsel compares to nvca.org models and term sheet.

requests.request: Deliver an officer's bring-down certificate covering reps (including national-security and OISP reps) and the completeness of side letters.
requests.format: Signed certificate.
requests.why: Changes between signing and closing.
requests.pass: No exceptions.
requests.fail: Exceptions not previously disclosed.

requests.request: Deliver evidence that cash will be held so that no more than one quarter of payroll is uninsured at any single bank (sweep agreements, second bank, Treasury MMF).
requests.format: Account agreements and post-funding allocation plan.
requests.why: Uninsured cash at one bank.
requests.pass: Allocation meets the treasury test at funding.
requests.fail: All proceeds into one bank above insured limits.

requests.request: Deliver waivers or amendments removing any strategic investor's veto over financing or M&A, or a documented pricing adjustment for it.
requests.format: Executed waiver or amendment.
requests.why: Catch-and-kill risk.
requests.pass: No strategic financing or M&A veto survives closing, or it is priced.
requests.fail: Veto remains unpriced.

requests.request: For late stage: deliver evidence of finance-function remediation (CFO and controller hired, auditor engaged, audit committee formed) if gaps were found.
requests.format: Offer letters, engagement letter, board resolution.
requests.why: FTX-type control gaps.
requests.pass: Remediation in place at closing or as a funded condition subsequent.
requests.fail: No remediation.

requests.request: Deliver quarterly the updated cohort file: customers acquired, active customers and orders per period.
requests.format: Production export.
requests.why: Deteriorating cohorts after investment.
requests.pass: Delivered each quarter; new cohorts at least as valuable as prior.
requests.fail: Late or missing; declining cohorts.

requests.request: Deliver quarterly ARR, NRR, GRR, CAC payback and burn multiple with the underlying customer-level file.
requests.format: Customer-level file and KPI pack.
requests.why: Metric drift and gaming.
requests.pass: Rebuilt metrics match the KPI pack within one point.
requests.fail: Differences or refusal of raw data.

requests.request: Deliver monthly management accounts and a quarterly treasury map with insured share by bank.
requests.format: Monthly pack; bank statements.
requests.why: Cash concentration and runway erosion.
requests.pass: Runway and treasury tests continue to pass.
requests.fail: Concentration above one quarter of payroll uninsured at one bank.

requests.request: Notify us of any new instrument issuance, side letter, financing proposal, insider round or exercise of an investor veto within five business days.
requests.format: Written notice with documents.
requests.why: Late-surfacing instruments and blocked financings.
requests.pass: Every event notified on time.
requests.fail: Events discovered after the fact.

requests.request: Deliver annual audited financial statements.
requests.format: Auditor-signed statements.
requests.why: Unaudited growth.
requests.pass: Unqualified opinion from a firm sized for the company.
requests.fail: Qualified opinion or auditor change.

requests.request: Deliver board materials and minutes under the information rights, including any repricing or down-round discussion.
requests.format: Board packs and signed minutes.
requests.why: Monitoring gap.
requests.pass: Delivered after each meeting.
requests.fail: Withheld materials.
requests.verify: Board observer or Management Rights Letter.

kill_tests.test: Any founder or contractor who created core IP has not assigned it to the company and will not sign a confirmatory assignment before closing.
Cap table cannot be reconciled to signed documents for every share, option, RSU, SAFE, warrant, convertible note and side letter before the term sheet.
Company refuses raw data-room access (contracts, billings, bank statements, cohort files) and asks investors to rely on deck metrics.
Company cannot or will not produce customers acquired and total active customers by period (and orders per period for non-subscription businesses).
Company will not let us contact named marquee customers, partners, validators or government users directly.
Core technical claim fails, or the company refuses, independent validation by our expert on our samples in our presence under a stated protocol.
Random sample of claimed users or customers fails live-activity testing in production systems, or the company refuses production access to our engineer.
Reported ARR or revenue cannot be traced to signed contracts, billings and bank deposits.

Late stage or secondary: no named CFO and controller with public- or audited-company experience, no independent audit, and a board wholly founder-controlled (FTX pattern), with no commitment to remediate before closing.

red_flags.flag: Founder will not give raw data-room access; 'trust the deck' metrics.
red_flags.check: Require read-only access to billing system, GL and bank portals; rebuild metrics ourselves.

red_flags.flag: Unreconciled cap table, or side letters surfacing late in the process.
red_flags.check: Reconcile every instrument to signed originals; obtain a company officer certificate that the side-letter list is complete.

red_flags.flag: One customer above 25% of revenue presented as ARR.
red_flags.check: Customer-level revenue file; contract term, renewal and termination rights for that customer; reference call with the customer.

red_flags.flag: No IP assignments from founders or contractors.
red_flags.check: Walk the full IP assignment chain against the contributor list from the code repository.

red_flags.flag: Company cannot or will not give customers acquired and active customers by period.
red_flags.check: Treat as a kill test; no valuation on fundamentals without the cohort file.

red_flags.flag: Investment case rests on founder charisma rather than data-room evidence.
red_flags.check: Score written materials and the data room with a fixed rubric and more than one rater before the live pitch.

red_flags.flag: Celebrity board with no domain experts; founder super-voting control with no sunset; no audit committee at late stage.
red_flags.check: Map voting control, board seats and each director's domain expertise; price super-voting without sunset as a risk item.

red_flags.flag: Named validators, partners or government users the company will not let us call.
red_flags.check: Call every named counterparty directly using contacts we source independently.

red_flags.flag: A strategic investor holding a veto over financing or M&A.
red_flags.check: Investor-rights map; require waiver or removal of the strategic's financing veto, or price catch-and-kill risk.

red_flags.flag: Insider-led round priced below the insiders' own recent marks or bridge terms, with a short decision window for non-participants.
red_flags.check: Run the insider-round checklist (2.11): conflicted directors, independent committee, price discovery, marks comparison, time and information for non-participants, minutes.

red_flags.flag: Revenue growth almost entirely from new-customer acquisition, with each new cohort worth less than the last.
red_flags.check: Share of revenue from customers acquired in the period; cumulative revenue per cohort by period since acquisition.

red_flags.flag: More than one quarter of payroll in uninsured deposits at one bank.
red_flags.check: Treasury map with insured share by institution; require sweeps, multiple banks or Treasury MMFs before funding.

red_flags.flag: Valuation justified by the last round, or by a theme at its media peak.
red_flags.check: Reprice against current comparables; compare entry valuation with sector history and the theme's media and fund-launch peak.

red_flags.flag: Model where margins expand with scale and no cost line is named.
red_flags.check: Line-by-line cost bridge, or hold margins flat.

red_flags.flag: NRR that excludes churned logos, or blended CAC that hides paid CAC.
red_flags.check: Recompute NRR/GRR from the raw cohort file including churned logos; compute paid CAC unblended by channel.

red_flags.flag: Lead investor spent a fraction of benchmark diligence effort (about 83 days, 118 hours, 10 reference calls).
red_flags.check: Do our own full diligence; do not treat the lead as a diligence anchor.

red_flags.flag: 'Proprietary deal' claimed with no account of who else saw it.
red_flags.check: Ask who else saw the round and whether competing term sheets exist.

red_flags.flag: A lead that concedes on liquidation preference or board control but fights on dividends.
red_flags.check: Ask why; atypical against the VC negotiability map.

red_flags.flag: Strategic or corporate VC counted on for follow-on support.
red_flags.check: Assume no CVC follow-on (median CVC life four years); review information, observer, ROFR and ROFN rights for technology leakage and exit blocking.

red_flags.flag: Exit thesis relies on a strategic acquirer with an overlapping product.
red_flags.check: Model antitrust scrutiny of sub-HSR deals and shelving risk; avoid milestone or earnout reliance.

red_flags.flag: Late-stage company with no controller, no internal audit, no complete employee list or customer assets held off balance sheet.
red_flags.check: Finance-function review; employee census reconciled to payroll; customer assets and liabilities on the balance sheet.

red_flags.flag: Runway shorter than 24 months to the next round.
red_flags.check: Rebuild monthly burn and test runway against the 616-day seed-to-A and 696-day between-round medians plus six months.

red_flags.flag: Employees raised internal warnings about the product or data (Theranos pattern).
red_flags.check: Ask for the internal complaints and whistleblower log; interview former employees.

metrics.metric: Rule of 40 (YoY ARR growth + FCF margin)
metrics.acceptable: 40% or more; primary screen only above about $25M ARR; one point of growth worth about 2x one point of FCF margin in valuation. Below about $25M ARR underwrite growth plus NRR/GRR and burn instead.
metrics.source: ICONIQ, State of Software 2025; ICONIQ Growth and Efficiency

metrics.acceptable: Median 38% in Q1 2026; target 50%+ above $10M ARR.

Just above 100% (2024 survey median NDR 101%). Sources conflict: v1 cites median about 117% in 2026 (networkcraft, cfoadvisors, WEAK, really a top-quartile figure). Benchmark the median on KeyBanc/Sapphire and the top-performer bar on Bessemer; a private company at 117% is top quartile, not average.
metrics.source: KeyBanc Capital Markets / Sapphire Ventures 2025 SaaS Survey

metrics.acceptable: Above 110% minimum, above 120% strong; median about 117% in 2026 (top-quartile public or late-stage figure, not a private median).

metrics.metric: NRR by ARR band, top performers (2021 vintage, refreshed 2024)
metrics.acceptable: $1M-$10M ARR: median 125% (top 145%+); $10M-$25M: 117%; $100M+: 115%. Zero-rate-era vintage: top-performer bar only.
Averages 85% to 90%; near 90% (KeyBanc/Sapphire); SMB can work at 70% to 80%.
Median 16 months for B2B SaaS in 2025 (IQR 10-24). Targets: SMB under 12 months, mid-market under 18, enterprise under 24; PLG under 12 months (WEAK).
metrics.source: Benchmarkit via Growth Unhinged (practitioner dataset); Bessemer; re-cap.com for PLG

metrics.acceptable: Under 12 months.
Above 0.75 is efficient.
Under 1.5x efficient; above 3x is trouble.
metrics.source: vcbeast.com (practitioner; originator Craft Ventures, no primary retrieved)

metrics.acceptable: Above 3:1 (partly replaced by Bessemer CLTV/CAC framing); recompute LTV from cohorts.
Long-run aim 65% to 70%; top performers 80%+ (Bessemer). v1 practitioner: above 70% to 75%.
About 20% projected for 2025 (15% in 2024).

metrics.metric: ARR growth by band, top performers (2021 vintage)
metrics.acceptable: $1M-$10M ARR: median 165% (top 230%+); $10M-$25M: 87%; $100M+: 57%. v1 (WEAK, re-cap.com): 100%+ early, 40% to 60% later.
Median 696 days between rounds; 616 days (about 20 months) seed to Series A (Q2 2025). Runway must cover at least 24 months to the next round.
metrics.source: Carta, State of Private Markets Q2 2025; Carta Series A Q2 2025

metrics.acceptable: About 17% of new rounds (Q3 2025); just over 19% (Q1 2025). Model a down round for any 2021-vintage mark.
Record $15.6M (Q2 2025); seed deal count down 25% YoY.
$47.9M (Q2 2025); Series A deal count down 18% YoY.
No single customer above 25% of revenue presented as ARR.

No more than one quarter of payroll in uninsured deposits at any one bank; balances above the $250,000 FDIC limit spread across banks, insured sweeps or Treasury MMFs. SVB reference: about 94% uninsured; $42B withdrawn March 9, 2023.
metrics.source: Metrick, JEP 2024; Song Ma, Yale Insights

metrics.acceptable: About 75% never return cash; 30% to 40% liquidate with investors losing most or all; 70% to 80% miss projected ROI; 90% to 95% miss a declared projection. Only one or two in ten VC investments succeed.
metrics.source: Ghosh, HBS Working Knowledge; Sorenson, Nanda and Samila, Yale Insights

metrics.acceptable: All-venture portfolio 1980-2006 about 22% IRR, generalized PME 1.44; dropping the best 5% makes risk-adjusted return negative.
metrics.source: Ouyang, Yu and Jagannathan, NBER w27690

metrics.acceptable: Ten-year top vs bottom quartile spread 43.2 points a year in venture (13.7 buyouts, about 0.5 fixed income).
Success about 30% after a prior success, 20% after a prior failure, 18% for first-timers (IPO or IPO filing, 1986-2003).
Average required 31% IRR; MOIC median 5.0x (mean 5.5x); marketed about 24% net IRR (median 20%) and 3.5x net MOIC (3.8x early, 2.8x late).

About 83 days first contact to close, about 118 hours of diligence, about 10 reference calls (13 late-stage firms, 8 early-stage). Doubling diligence worth 2% to 6% of capital invested (model, abstract-level).
metrics.source: Gompers et al. 2020; Fu and Taylor, NBER w33987

metrics.acceptable: About 100 opportunities considered per closed deal (151 IT, 78 healthcare); 1.7 term sheets issued per closed deal.
More than 30% professional networks, about 30% self-generated, about 20% other investors, 10% inbound, 8% portfolio referrals.
Realized outcomes fell inside CFOs' 80% confidence intervals only 36% of the time: widen management ranges about 2x.
None on average: 6,103 IPO firms, median real sales growth above 8% a year, cost-to-sales did not fall. Hold margins flat unless a named cost line falls.
metrics.source: Thomas, Ertan and Lewellen, Yale Insights

metrics.acceptable: Above-average pitch factor about 35% more likely funded, then worse follow-on and survival; all-women teams 7x more sensitive to delivery.
metrics.source: Song Ma and Allen Hu, Yale Insights

metrics.acceptable: Thematic ETFs lose about 30% risk-adjusted over first five years.
metrics.source: Ben-David, Franzoni, Kim and Moussawi, RFS 2023

metrics.acceptable: Median CVC lasts four years (10 to 12 for traditional VC).
About 6% (6.4% in working paper) of pharma acquisitions; clustered below HSR thresholds; up to 50 a year.
1x non-participating is founder-friendly and acceptable; 2x participating is not.
Broad-based weighted average is standard; full ratchet is punitive.
Unicorns from about 40 (2013) to 1,500+; median age at IPO 9 to 13 years (2012-2024); 12(g) trigger raised from 500 to 2,000 holders.
New direct flight to a portfolio company: 1.0 to 1.4 points more likely to IPO or exit successfully.

Team important to 95% and most important to 47%; business model 83%; product 74%; market 68%; valuation fifth. Team cited in 96% of successes and 92% of failures: the founder workstream gets the most hours.

Diligence against the version in force at signing. Two sources: v1 says NVCA updated five models in October 2025 (tranched financing, national-security reps) and revised the ROFR (April 2026) and voting agreement (June 2026) (1752.vc, aggregator, WEAK); nvca.org now lists the core financing set as Updated November 2026, plus a July 2020 LPA CFIUS insert and 2025 model PIPE sets.
Yale 20-year venture IRR 165.9% vs time-weighted 24.6% (to June 2018). Never compound an IRR; use PME.

third_party_reports.report: Technology and security diligence (code, architecture, security posture, open-source license exposure)
third_party_reports.provider: Tech and security diligence firm engaged by us
third_party_reports.required_when: Series A and later; any round where the product is the asset

third_party_reports.report: Quality of earnings (agreed-upon procedures or consulting engagement, no assurance; scope per 5.5)
third_party_reports.required_when: Growth-stage rounds (Series B and later) and secondaries

hard_questions.question: Show the cohort data behind NRR, by month.
hard_questions.good_answer: A raw monthly customer-level file, including churned logos, from which we reproduce reported NRR and GRR within a point and tie cohort revenue to billings.

hard_questions.question: Which founders or contractors have NOT assigned IP?
hard_questions.good_answer: A named list (ideally empty) checked against the repository contributor list, with executed assignments or confirmatory assignments for every gap before closing.

hard_questions.question: What is paid CAC, unblended, and the payback by segment?
hard_questions.good_answer: Paid CAC by channel and segment from ad-platform and payroll data, with payback per segment inside the SMB under 12, mid-market under 18 and enterprise under 24 month targets.

hard_questions.question: What is the real cash position and the default-alive runway?
hard_questions.good_answer: Bank-confirmed cash and a monthly burn schedule showing runway of at least 24 months, or a default-alive path to breakeven without new capital.

hard_questions.question: How many customers did you acquire each quarter, and how many are active today? Show orders per period.
hard_questions.good_answer: Quarterly acquired, active and orders counts produced immediately from the production database, reconciling to revenue.

hard_questions.question: Name each specific cost line that falls as a share of revenue, and why.
hard_questions.good_answer: A line-by-line cost bridge with contracts or supplier quotes, or an admission that the base case holds margins flat.

hard_questions.question: At today's price and fully diluted count, what margin and growth must be true at steady state?
hard_questions.good_answer: A reverse-valuation worksheet on the fully diluted count (options, RSUs, warrants, SAFEs) with steady-state margin and growth that are achievable against public comparables.

hard_questions.question: Who can block the next financing or a sale, and has anyone ever used that right?
hard_questions.good_answer: A complete investor-rights map with holders of every veto and a history of every use, with no strategic holding a financing veto.

hard_questions.question: If your bank closed this morning, how many weeks of payroll could you meet?
hard_questions.good_answer: At least a quarter's payroll in insured or diversified balances available same day, with backup banking relationships in place.

hard_questions.question: May we call every named validator, partner and government user directly?
hard_questions.good_answer: Yes, with contacts we may source independently.

hard_questions.question: What did your founders' prior companies actually return to investors, per the cap table?
hard_questions.good_answer: Cap tables or filings for prior companies showing actual distributions that match the bio.

hard_questions.question: At the current 616-day seed-to-A cadence, does the runway reach the next round with six months to spare?
hard_questions.good_answer: Runway of at least 26 to 27 months from close (616 days plus six months), or a milestone plan that reaches breakeven.

hard_questions.question: Who on the board is conflicted in this round, and is there an independent committee?
hard_questions.good_answer: A conflicts schedule and an independent committee with its own advisors that approved the price.

hard_questions.question: What third-party price discovery was run (outside lead, competing term sheets)?
hard_questions.good_answer: Evidence of an outside lead or competing term sheets, with the reasons any higher-valuation alternative was set aside.

hard_questions.question: How does the price compare with each insider's latest fund mark and any bridge conversion terms?
hard_questions.good_answer: A table of each insider's latest mark and bridge terms showing the round is not priced below them, or a documented reason.

hard_questions.question: How long do non-participants have to decide, what information do they get, and what happens to them (pay-to-play, conversion to common, preference stacking)?
hard_questions.good_answer: Weeks not days, the same data room as insiders, and no punitive conversion without a fair-price record.

hard_questions.question: What do the minutes record on alternatives considered?
hard_questions.good_answer: Minutes listing every alternative, its terms and why it was rejected.

hard_questions.question: What makes this company different from the base rate that about 75% of VC-backed companies never return cash?
hard_questions.good_answer: Specific, evidenced differences (retention, unit economics, technical validation) rather than team charisma.

hard_questions.question: What is the lead's and co-investors' track record without their top one or two outcomes, and are the partners who earned it still there?
hard_questions.good_answer: Deal-level track record by leading partner, shown with and without top outcomes, using PME rather than compounded IRR.

hard_questions.question: Who else saw this round?
hard_questions.good_answer: Names of other investors approached and any competing term sheets.

failure_cases.what_happened: Raised about $700M (KaW 2018) or close to $1B at a $9B valuation (HLS Forum 2022; Untamed Unicorns 2026); sources differ. 2014 revenue projected at $100M; actual just over $100,000. The analyzer promised about 200 tests ran about a dozen; tests ran on third-party analyzers. Unauthorized pharma logos; claimed DoD medevac use that never happened. Founder 100 votes per share; board of former officials with no lab expertise; internal warnings ignored; investors invested on relationship.
failure_cases.check: Independent technical validation by our expert on our samples in our presence; call every named validator, partner and government user; error rates, complaint logs, regulator correspondence; reconcile projections to invoices and cash; treat celebrity board without domain experts and founder super-voting as red flags; no investment on relationship without audited financials and data-room access.

failure_cases.what_happened: Founder claimed 4.25M users when Frank had about 300,000 and generated a synthetic list of 4M+ fake customers. JPMorgan paid $175M; about 70% of 400,000 emails bounced. 85-month sentence; restitution over $287M; judge criticized JPMorgan's diligence.
failure_cases.check: Never accept a user list as evidence; test a random sample for live activity (logins, transactions, deliverable email) through production systems with our own engineer present.

failure_cases.what_happened: Growth bought with marketing; about 70% of acquired customers churned within six months; declining cumulative net revenue per cohort. IPO range cut from $15-$17 to $10; shares later fell about 70% more.
CBCV under $10 per share while the stock traded around $64; growth 'made entirely of acquisition'; repeat rates below Amazon's two decades earlier; stock fell about 10% the day the paper posted.
failure_cases.check: Share of revenue from newly acquired customers by period; repeat-purchase curve against the category leader.

failure_cases.what_happened: Raised $400M at $32B, up from $25B six months earlier, before collapse. Nearly $2B from VCs with no internal audit, no accounting department, no complete employee list, customer deposits off the main balance sheet.
failure_cases.check: Controls first: in-house CFO and controller, employee census reconciled to payroll, customer assets and liabilities on the balance sheet, independent audit; last round is not validation.

failure_cases.what_happened: Hundreds of startups held large uninsured balances at SVB (about 94% uninsured deposits), threatening payroll; $42B withdrawn on March 9, 2023.
failure_cases.check: Treasury map: balances by bank, insured share, single-bank covenants; weeks of payroll if the bank closed.

failure_cases.case: Zync v. Porsche (Del. Ch., pleading stage)
failure_cases.what_happened: Porsche's venture arm held 5% via a $2.9M note, one of three board seats and a debt-approval right; its designee voted down a $10M Series A, withheld a promised bridge after obtaining a confidential competitor agreement, and conditioned a $50M PE offer on indemnities. Company shut down. Disloyalty, aiding-and-abetting and implied-covenant claims survived.
failure_cases.check: Investor-rights map of every veto over financing and M&A and its holder; treat a strategic with a financing veto as a red flag.

failure_cases.case: Footprint (Guilbeau v. Footprint, Del. Ch., pleading stage)
failure_cases.what_happened: Near-insolvent company raised $500M Class F preferred, $450M from three insider funds with board designees, at a pre-money about half their own bridge-implied value; higher alternatives set aside; Class A holders given three weeks; disclosures omitted valuation and insider benefits. Entire fairness applied; aiding-and-abetting claims survived.
failure_cases.check: Price insider rounds against insiders' own marks and bridges; document rejected alternatives; give non-participants real time and data; disclose insider benefits.

failure_cases.what_happened: Irreversible early commitments made before demand was validated; cited with excessive funding as a driver of the largest venture failures.
failure_cases.check: Stage capital to validated demand; test cohort and demand evidence before funding irreversible build-out.

failure_cases.what_happened: Stripe reported raising about $4B at about $55B, roughly half its 2021 $95B valuation; FTX's $32B mark preceded collapse.
failure_cases.check: Reprice any 2021-vintage mark against current comparables; model a down round; value the specific security.

failure_cases.what_happened: Named as other recent late-stage fraud convictions in HLS Forum, Untamed Unicorns, 2026; no further detail in source.
failure_cases.check: Independent technical validation and direct counterparty confirmation; late-stage finance-function and governance requirements.
